pr_title: Autosize inspector property editors rather than always being half-half with label
pr_body:
Closes #7133
Closes #35564

This resolves a (seemingly longstanding) issue where the editor inspector always splits Property Editors and their Labels 50/50 no matter what. Most of the time it would be beneficial to have a better view of the Property Editor, especially for long strings or paths.

Demo:
Note that the width of the label is capped at 50%, so the property editor does not become tiny.
![inspector_autosize](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41730826/90631810-bb970680-e266-11ea-9a9e-3cccdbb4ad04.gif)

Works everywhere inspector is used, as expected.
![inspector_autosize_projsettings](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41730826/90631839-c5206e80-e266-11ea-8ce5-130d607c6f46.gif)

This also maintains a form of "backwards compatibility" with the Animation Blend Tree Editor and the Visual Shader Editor, which both used the previous setting, which was `set_name_split_ratio()` . The method (and associated property) is now `label_target_width`, so setting it to 0 has the same effect in both cases, requiring no other changes.
pr_comments:
After we discussion on IRC it was decided that this is a good solution if a few tweaks are made.

Firstly, if the maximum label length is some small fraction of the total inspector width, the ratio will be set to 0.5. This is to avoid very wide property editors, such as in the editor settings.

Secondly, it may also be worth having a general limit on the ratio. I would need to play with the limit values in this case to see how it looks.

```
[09:50:12] <Akien> I don't mind the disalignment in different categories/tabs, but it's true that in the GIF for some of them the new split is too much
[09:50:25] <Akien> If the property names are small, the value field ends up huge
[09:50:41] <Calinou> the value field could have a maximum width, maybe
[09:50:56] <Akien> There should be some more advanced logic to make it reasonably sized based on the width available (hence ratio :))
[09:51:06] <Groud> Also, it's pretty bad that it can lead to input boxes so wide... it makes the little up/down arrow very far from the value
[09:52:26] <EricEzaM[m]> also the misalignment between tabs and categories already existed
[09:53:09] <EricEzaM[m]> oh wait sorry, the labels? I thought the editors
[09:53:14] <EricEzaM[m]> the editors were not aligned
[09:53:54] <EricEzaM[m]> oh wait never mind lol, the labels too. In 3.2.2 stable they are not aligned between groups and categories
[09:54:42] <Groud> I don't know, I'd say we need a smarter solution IMHO
[09:55:21] <Groud> I'd say that, when the label is too long to fit, the value should shrink
[09:55:44] <Akien> IMO for wide panels the 50/50 split is fine to keep. It's not the best but shrinking all the way down to the max property name length is too much if it makes gigantic input fields
[09:56:09] <Akien> The original issue is mostly about the Inspector dock, which is narrow and where it can actually be problematic that the 50/50 split doesn't allow for wider input boxes
[09:56:57] <Akien> And then in the inspector, there's usually so many properties that calculating where the split should be based on all of them might not help much, as there will likely be both short and long properties names
[09:57:15] <Akien> So it's a tricky one :)
[09:57:37] <EricEzaM[m]> Also I think it would look pretty bad not having the field/editor width the same between properties. Very visually messy
[09:57:45] <Akien> Yeah
[09:58:15] <Akien> But if we do go for a solution like this PR, then I think it should have some clamping to e.g. [0.4, 0.6] ratio.
[09:58:39] <EricEzaM[m]> built in ratio or customisable via method
[09:59:09] <Akien> And if the container size is bigger than X times the min size of the EditorProperty, then it should just use 0.5.
[10:00:13] <Akien> (i.e. in a wide EditorSettings, no need for a specific ratio. But if it's shrinked to a size where it makes sense to give more space for input fields, then the ratio can be applied (and thus it would always be applied in the Inspector dock, unless people expand it to a very large width).
[10:01:18] <EricEzaM[m]> Yeah that makes sense to me
[10:11:05] <EricEzaM[m]> hmmm but you would also want some sort of override since a value of zero is used in animation blend tree and visual shader editor
[10:11:44] <EricEzaM[m]> You don't want to clamp those, and you want them to ignore the _"size is bigger than X times the min size of the EditorProperty, then it should just use 0.5."_ rule
```

@akien-mga @groud
After the discussion above I have implemented:
* Editor min width of 50%
* Editor max width of 70%
* If label width is smaller than 30% of total width, the editor width is set to 50%.
* I added an additional property to determine if the editor property should be forced to use the target width. This is useful in cases like in animation blend tree and visual shader editor where we don't want the above limits to be applied.

Here is what it looks like now.
![new_inspector_autosize](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41730826/92991674-f409c780-f528-11ea-85a3-6c35338f32c2.gif)

As per [this UI revamp mockup](https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/nhsqug/ui_rewamp_just_for_fun_what_do_you_think/), I wonder if we should right-align property names in inspectors that are wide enough. This would especially make sense in the Project Settings and Editor Settings.

Either way, that can be considered for a future PR – I'm just throwing the idea out there.

> As per this UI revamp mockup, I wonder if we should right-align property names in inspectors that are wide enough

Hmm, I don't know. On the one hand it makes the property name closer to the property, which is good, but on the other hand I find it harder to read the list of properties one after the other. It kind of makes it more difficult to find the properties you are looking for IMHO.

I think that in general, the compact form is more common than the expanded one. It's good to make things work well when expanded, but I see little reasons why someone you need to expand the inspector if all information they need is already visible.
So I think keeping things ragged left is maybe better for this case.

For the project and editor settings, my opinion is that maybe we should find a way to reduce the space taken by the properties's name instead of ragging them right. My idea would be to shorten the name, but find a way to set up longer description for them (guess it would appear as a popup maybe?).
Just like @groud I am also concerned about readability here, so I am not entirely sure if there is enough consensus for this to go forward.

Was about to make an issue about this, but then i saw it hasn't been merged yet, maybe thats why the resizing dosen't work :P
i think this is a good QOL change, because to be fair this does not look good :/ 
![Skärmbild 2021-12-30 125432](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13393087/147749780-9e87f441-5ed6-4fc7-9a62-aaa90acf6ac5.png)
![Skärmbild 2021-12-30 125152](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13393087/147749787-aee4390b-4276-4ba2-b201-026a39e3505a.png)
![Skärmbild 2021-12-30 125015](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13393087/147749794-82f34302-778c-4ceb-b737-6027ee4ac50b.png)

We've discussed this a few times over the years and were never really convinced that this really improves usability.

It would be better to have it behave like SplitContainer where you can drag the separation one way or another as needed. So closing for now, but some of the code here might be relevant to salvage for a future implementation.

issue_context.title: Debugger: variables monitor sections size
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 rc3

**OS/device including version:**
Win 10

**Issue description:**

Once upon a time we had tiny displays, when I start working as an IT, I had a 13" inch one, it was cool, lacks of space to show things made all the debugging work funny and really crowded...
Now we use to work on 24" and bigger displays, at home we have even 34" widescreen displays... and we still have all crowded because the Debugger Variables Monitor puts a lot of effort in wasting free space for variable "names" section instead of making "value" section bigger and helping coders debugging long-value strings with easer! 
😄 😄 😄 😄 😄 😄 😄 😄 

Just kidding, but for real, we have big monitors, correct column size please: smaller "variable name" column and wider "variable value" column

![immagine](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47447512/73127905-b40cc900-3fc7-11ea-9484-28865734a8b9.png)
comments:
> Just kidding, but for real, we have big monitors, correct column size please: 

Not everyone does. We need to make sure the debugger is still usable in smaller displays, as many people use Godot on laptops.

The problem is not the debugger. It uses the EditorInspector class, which divides the space into two equal columns.

![200126-1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/73134274-b877c700-4045-11ea-9b00-7c98cca2a662.png)

If you add the ability to change the column width in the Inspector, then the problem with the debugger will be solved automatically.
